The first release of RTXUI: a C++23 terminal UI library that runs a
browser-style pipeline. Write the interface in HTML, style it with CSS, bind
it to plain C++ members, and the screen follows when they change.

### What it does

- **Layout:** flexbox, grid (`minmax()`, `repeat(auto-fill)`, named lines and
  areas), positioning with `sticky`, scroll containers, `@media` queries,
  `calc()` and custom properties, tables with `colspan`/`rowspan`.
- **Motion:** transitions on colors, sizes, opacity and `translate`, and
  `@keyframes` animations.
- **Interaction:** mouse hover, click, drag and wheel; Tab order and arrow-key
  spatial navigation; text selection and copy; OSC 8 hyperlinks.
- **Built-in elements:** `<input>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>`, `<checkbox>`,
  `<radio>`, `<slider>`, `<progress>`, `<tabs>`, `<details>`, `<dialog>`,
  `<toast>`, `<tooltip>`, `<markdown>`, and virtual lists of any length.
- **C++:** `Bind()` members, methods and collections; `<if>`, `<for>`, slots
  and props for your own components; `PostTask()` from timers and threads;
  optional C++26 reflection for struct fields.
- **Development:** hot reload of templates and styles, diagnostics with line
  and column, `RTXUI_STRICT=1` to abort on any of them, and headless rendering
  for tests.

### Where it runs

Linux (GCC 14+, Clang 18+), macOS (AppleClang), Windows (MSVC, clang-cl,
MinGW-w64) and the browser (Emscripten). It needs C++23 and depends on nothing
beyond the standard library.

### Getting it

```cmake
include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(rtxui
  GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/ArthurSonzogni/RTXUI.git
  GIT_TAG        v0.1.0)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(rtxui)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE rtxui)
```

`find_package(rtxui)` and `pkg-config rtxui` work after `cmake --install`, and
the repository is a Bazel module (`@rtxui`). Attached: the source tarball,
prebuilt Linux x64 and macOS universal packages, and their SHA256SUMS.

### Compatibility

This is a 0.x release: 0.2 may change the API and the ABI, and its notes will
say what to write instead. Patch releases keep both. See
[Compatibility](https://arthursonzogni.github.io/RTXUI/guide/compatibility).

Documentation and 66 live examples:
https://arthursonzogni.github.io/RTXUI/
